title: Colorado PUC Decision R26-0079-I: Interim Decision Addressing Remaining Interventions
text:
Decision No. R26-0079-I 
BEFORE THE PUBLIC UTILITIES COMMISSION OF THE STATE OF COLORADO 
PROCEEDING NO. 25A-0472CP-EXT 
IN THE MATTER OF THE APPLICATION OF BRECKDIRECT LLC DOING BUSINESS AS 
PEAK 1 EXPRESS AND/OR PEAK ONE EXPRESS FOR PERMANENT AUTHORITY TO 
EXTEND OPERATIONS UNDER CERTIFICATE OF PUBLIC CONVENIENCE AND 
NECESSITY NO. 55937. 
INTERIM DECISION 
ADDRESSING REMAINING INTERVENTIONS 
Issued Date: February 4, 2026 
I. 
STATEMENT AND SUMMARY 
1. 
This Decision acknowledges Aspire Tours LLC (“Aspire”) as an intervener of right 
(and party) to this Proceeding and rejects the Intervention filed by Ullr Tours LLC, doing business 
as The Colorado Sightseer (“Colorado Sightseer”). 
II. 
PROCEDURAL HISTORY1 
2. 
On November 5, 2025, BreckDirect, LLC, doing business as Peak 1 Express 
(“Applicant”), initiated this matter by filing the above-captioned Application, which it later 
amended (“Amended Application”).2 
3. 
The Amended Application seeks to extend operations under Certificate of Public 
Convenience and Necessity (“CPCN”) Permit No. 55937 to provide call-and-demand sightseeing 
service between all points in the Counties of Boulder, Clear Creek, Denver, Jefferson, Larimer, 
Park, and Summitt, Colorado.3 

1 Only the procedural history necessary to understand this Decision is included. 
2 See Application filed November 5, 2025; Amended Application filings made on November 10, 
2025; Decision No. R26-0027-I at 21 (issued January 14, 2026). 
3 See Amended Application at 3 and 5; Attachment to Amended Application.

2 
4. 
On November 17, 2025, the Colorado Public Utilities Commission 
(“Commission”) provided public notice of the Amended Application and established a 30-day 
intervention deadline.4 
5. 
As relevant here, on November 19, 2025, Epic Charter LLC, doing business as Red 
Rocks Shuttle (“Epic”) filed a “Notice of Intervention by Right, Alternative Motion for 
Intervention, Entry of Appearance . . .” and a copy of its Commission-issued Letter of Authority. 
6. 
On November 24, 2025, Aspire filed a “Petition for Intervention and Entry of 
Appearance” (“Aspire’s Intervention”) and a copy of Denver Cannabis Tours’ (“Denver 
Cannabis”) Commission-issued Letter of Authority (“Denver Cannabis’ Authority”).5 
7. 
On December 16, 2025, CKIMY, LLC doing business as iLIMO (“iLIMO”) filed 
an “Intervention & Entry of Appearance” and a copy of its Commission-issued Letters of 
Authority.6 
8. 
On December 17, 2025, Colorado Sightseer filed its “Intervention and Entry of 
Appearance as a Matter of Right . . .” (“Colorado Sightseer’s Intervention”). It did not file a copy 
of its Commission-issued Letter of Authority with its Intervention. 
9. 
On December 23, 2025, the Commission deemed the Amended Application 
complete and referred this matter to an Administrative Law Judge (“ALJ”) by minute entry. 
10. 
As relevant here, on January 14, 2026, the ALJ acknowledged Epic and iLIMO as 
intervening parties and established a January 29, 2026 deadline by which Aspire and Colorado

Sightseer must file copies of their Commission-issued Letters of Authority.7 At the same time, the 
ALJ noted that a decision on Aspire’s and Colorado Sightseer’s Interventions would be deferred 
until after the deadline to file their Letters of Authority.8 
11. 
On January 28, 2026, Aspire filed a copy of its Commission-issued Letter of 
Authority for its CPCN Permit No. 55865. 
12. 
On January 29, 2026, Colorado Sightseer filed Commission Decision No. C17-
0584 (issued July 18, 2017) in Proceeding No. 17A-0330CP-TRANSFER (“the Decision” or 
“Decision No. C17-0584”). Colorado Sightseer did not file a copy of its Commission-issued Letter 
of Authority. 
III. 
FINDINGS AND CONCLUSIONS 
A. 
Relevant Law 
13. 
To intervene of right in a proceeding such as this, an intervention must: include a 
copy of the common carrier’s letter of authority; show that the carrier’s authority is in good 
standing; identify the specific parts of the authority that are in conflict with the application; and 
explain the consequences to the carrier and the public interest if the application is granted.9 An 
intervener’s letter of authority provides the basis for the legally protected right which an intervener 
claims may be impacted by the proceeding. Thus, when determining whether an intervention of 
right is appropriate, it is important to determine whether the intervener’s letter of authority shows 
that it has the right to operate in a manner that may be impacted by an application’s requested 
authority. Indeed, the incumbent carrier’s legally protected interest in an application proceeding 

7 Decision No. R26-0027-I at 22. 
8 Id. 
9 Rule 1401(f), of the Commission’s Rules of Practice and Procedure, 4 Code of Colorado 
Regulations (“CCR”) 723-1. See § 40-6-109(a), C.R.S.; and RAM Broadcasting of Colo. Inc., v. Pub. Utils. 
Comm’n, 702 P.2d 746, 749 (Colo. 1985). 

Before the Public Utilities Commission of the State of Colorado 
Decision No. R26-0079-I 
Proceeding No. 25A-0472CP-EXT 
4 
arises from its property interest in its CPCN permit. The Commission has essentially codified this 
principle through the intervention of right standards in Rule 1401(f)(I), 4 CCR 723-1. 
B. 
Aspire’s Intervention 
14. 
Aspire argues that it has a legal protected right in the subject of this Proceeding 
because the proposed authority overlaps with its authority.10 In support, Aspire states that its CPCN 
Permit No. 55865 gives it authority transport passengers in call-and-demand sightseeing service 
in the Counties of Boulder, Denver, Clear Creek, Jefferson, Larimer, Summit and Park, Colorado, 
which overlap with the authority sought here.11 Aspire asserts that it is willing and able to provide 
the proposed service; it is able to handle a substantial greater volume of traffic; it has sufficient 
equipment and capacity to meet the public’s needs; there is no unmet need for the proposed service; 
and that granting the Application may divert traffic from and endanger its investments.12 
15. 
Consistent with Decision No. R26-0027-I, Aspire filed a copy of its Commission-
issued Letter of Authority, CPCN Permit No. 55865 on January 28, 2026. Its Letter of Authority 
confirms that it is authorized to provide transportation service as stated in its Intervention. The 
ALJ finds that Aspire’s Intervention and Letter of Authority establish that its CPCN Permit No. 
55865 overlaps or conflicts with Applicant’s requested authority and otherwise meets Rule 
1401(f)’s requirements.13 As such, the ALJ acknowledges Aspire as a party to this Proceeding. 
C. 
Colorado Sightseer’s Intervention 
16. 
Decision No. R26-0027-I requires Colorado Sightseer to file a copy of its 
Commission-issued Letter of Authority by January 29, 2026, and warns that if it fails to do so, the 

10 See Aspire’s Intervention at 1. 
11 Id. 
12 Id. at 1. 
13 See Rule 1401(f), 4 CCR 723-1. 

Before the Public Utilities Commission of the State of Colorado 
Decision No. R26-0079-I 
Proceeding No. 25A-0472CP-EXT 
5 
ALJ will decide whether Colorado Sightseer may intervene based on the record, which may result 
in a decision rejecting Colorado Sightseer’s Intervention and not allowing it party status in this 
Proceeding.14 Colorado Sightseer did not file a copy of its Letter of Authority, but instead filed 
Decision No. C17-0584. The ALJ will decide Colorado Sightseer’s request to intervene based on 
the record. 
17. 
Colorado Sightseer seeks to intervene as of right.15 It asserts that it may intervene 
as of right because its CPCN Permit No. 54166 authorizes it to provide service in areas that overlap 
with the proposed authority, giving it a legally protected right that may be impacted if the proposed 
authority is granted.16 Specifically, Colorado Sightseer states that its Permit No. 54166 authorizes 
it to transport passengers in sightseeing service between hotels with a minimum of 50 rooms 
located in the Counties of Adam, Arapahoe, Boulder, Denver, Douglas, and Jefferson, Colorado 
on the one hand, and all points in the Counties of Adams, Arapahoe, Broomfield, Boulder, Denver, 
Douglas, Jefferson, Alamosa, Clear Creek, El Paso, Fremont, Grand, Larimer, Park, Pueblo, 
Saguache, Summit, and Teller, Colorado, on the other hand.17 
18. 
Because Colorado Sightseer did not file a copy of its Commission-issued Letter of 
Authority, the record does not confirm that it has authority in good standing that overlaps or 
conflicts with the authority sought here. Filing Decision No. C17-0584 does not remedy this. The 
Decision approves an Application seeking to transfer CPCN Permit No. 54166 to Colorado 
Sightseer.18 Decision No. C17-0584 includes no information outlining the scope of the authority 
that was transferred. Indeed, although Decision No. C17-0584 states that CPCN Permit No. 54166 

14 Decision No. R26-0027-I at 13-14. 
15 Colorado Sightseer’s Intervention at 1. 
16 See id. 
17 Id. 
18 Decision No. C17-0584 at 2. 

Before the Public Utilities Commission of the State of Colorado 
Decision No. R26-0079-I 
Proceeding No. 25A-0472CP-EXT 
6 
“is set forth in the Appendix attached to this Decision,” Colorado Sightseer did not file the 
Appendix that was attached to the Decision.19 Notably, the Decision conditionally grants the 
Application, provided that Colorado Sightseer meets certain requirements in the Decision within 
60 days of the Decision’s effective date.20 If the Decision’s requirements were not met by the 
established deadline, the Decision provides that “. . . the approval to transfer CPCN PUC No. 
54166 shall be void.”21 There is no information in the record indicating that Colorado Sightseer 
met those requirements and was ultimately issued a Letter of Authority. 
19. 
The ALJ gave Colorado Sightseer an opportunity to cure the defect with its 
Intervention by filing its Commission-issued Letter of Authority, but it failed to do so. Filing its 
Letter of Authority is not a burden on Colorado Sightseer or any intervener given that motor 
carriers operating under their authority should have their authority readily at hand. Indeed, motor 
carriers intervening in Application proceedings regularly file their Letters of Authority with their 
interventions, as required by Rule 1401(f)(I), 4 CCR 723-1. Colorado Sightseer has failed to 
establish good cause for its failure to file its Letter of Authority. Nor has it requested that the ALJ 
waive the requirement to file its Letter of Authority (or provided good cause therefore). 
20. 
Colorado Sightseer was warned that failing to file its Letter of Authority will result 
in the ALJ deciding its Intervention based on the record and may result in a decision rejecting 
Colorado Sightseer’s Intervention and not allowing it party status in this Proceeding.22 By failing 
to file a copy of its Letter of Authority, Colorado Sightseer assumed the risk that its Intervention 

19 Arguably, this means that Colorado Sightseer failed to even file a complete copy of the referenced 
Decision. 
20 Id. at 3. The Decision also notes that the Commission may grant additional time for compliance 
for good cause shown if a request for more time is filed within 60 days. Id. 
21 Id. 
22 Decision No. R26-0027-I at 14. 

Before the Public Utilities Commission of the State of Colorado 
Decision No. R26-0079-I 
Proceeding No. 25A-0472CP-EXT 
7 
would be rejected. Even so, the ALJ viewed Decision No. C17-0584 in a light most favorable to 
Colorado Sightseer. As explained above, that Decision does not establish that Colorado Sightseer 
owns a Letter of Authority that gives it a legally protected interest that entitles it to intervene as a 
matter of right in this Proceeding. It cannot stand as a substitute for Rule 1401(f)(I)’s mandatory 
requirement that an intervener of right file a copy of its Commission-issued Letter of Authority. 
For the reasons discussed, the ALJ concludes that Colorado Sightseer has failed to meet the 
requirements to intervene as of right under Rule 1401(f)(I), 4 CCR 723-1 because it did not file a 
copy of its Letter of Authority. As such, Colorado Sightseer’s Intervention is rejected and it is not 
a party to this Proceeding. 
21. 
Consistent with the above discussion and Decision No. R26-0027-I, the parties to 
this Proceeding are Applicant, Epic, iLIMO, and Aspire. 
IV. 
ORDER 
A. 
It Is Ordered That: 
1. 
Aspire Tours LLC is acknowledged as a party to this Proceeding, consistent with 
the above discussion. 
2. 
Consistent with the above discussion, the “Intervention and Entry of Appearance as 
a Matter of Right to Application of a Transportation Utility” that Ullr LLC, doing business as The 
Colorado Sightseer (“Colorado Sightseer”) filed on December 17, 2025 is rejected. Colorado 
Sightseer is not a party to this Proceeding.
